records.name: FIDE (Dutch) System, 2026 edition
records.scope_note: Pairing algorithm only. Tournament setup, standings, score valuation, result correction and publication remain caller/arbiter responsibilities.
limitations: Exact search has declared deterministic ceilings; exhaustion is a typed failure, not a conformance result.
C8 look-ahead is limited to the next bracket and is a documented implementation strategy.
Some rule readings and complete per-system independent verification remain open (G-11).

records.name: Dubov System, 2026 edition
records.scope_note: Pairing algorithm only. Ratings, TPN assignment/recalculation, score histories and event facts are supplied by the caller.
limitations: Per-system behavior has not been independently established for every clause or input family.
Bounded-search exhaustion returns a typed error; no partial pairing is published.

records.name: Burstein System, 2026 edition
records.scope_note: Pairing procedure only. Pairing-Core does not calculate the C.04.4.2 Index. After seeding, the caller must supply a complete, finite, provenance-labelled C.04 Index set; missing values are rejected.
limitations: No local C.04 Burstein Index calculation is implemented.
C.07 Buchholz/Sonneborn-Berger implementations are not assumed equivalent to C.04.4.2 values or unplayed-round rules.
The external value producer's semantics and tournament-state correctness remain caller obligations.

records.name: Lim System, 2026 edition
records.scope_note: Pairing algorithm only. Maxi-tournament rating premises and tournament-management facts are caller-owned.
limitations: Some upward-scrutiny and ordering readings remain under audit.
No independent full-system conformance evidence has been established.

records.name: Double-Swiss System, 2026 edition
records.scope_note: Pairing procedure only. Match results, forfeits, points and their standings valuation are caller-owned inputs.
limitations: Next-bracket look-ahead and search ordering are implementation strategies, not independent proof of full rule equivalence.
No independent full-system conformance evidence has been established.

records.name: Swiss Team Pairing System, 2026 edition
records.scope_note: Teams are pairing units. Team composition, lineups, match/game point valuation, primary/secondary score policy, team TPNs and roster management remain caller-owned.
limitations: Type A/B/none colour preferences are represented, but complete per-clause independent verification remains open.
Next-bracket look-ahead and search ordering are implementation strategies, not independent proof of full rule equivalence.

records.name: Olympiad Pairing Rules, 2022 edition
records.scope_note: Dated event-specific team pairing procedure. Event administration, team presence/eligibility and board lineup management are not provided.
limitations: Independent per-system evidence is incomplete; see G-11 and the remaining partial, disputed, and out-of-scope clauses.
The source/effective date is retained as 2022-01-01; this is not silently promoted to a 2026 C.04 system.
Source currentness is unknown: the 2022 chapter and effective date were retrieved, but the search is bounded and does not prove no later Olympiad rules exist.

records.name: Baku Acceleration helper, 2026 edition
records.scope_note: Pure helper functions for GA/GB and virtual-point inputs. Pairing-Core does not select an acceleration policy, manage late entries, verify scoring premises, or manage tournament standings.
limitations: Caller is responsible for correct event eligibility, late-entry history and applying the helper to the intended Swiss system.
Only the source's worked examples and selected helper behavior have regression fixtures.

records.name: Berger round-robin tables, C.05 Annex 1
records.scope_note: Generates the published Berger schedule for field sizes 3–16 and supports double-cycle colour swapping. It is a fixed schedule, not a searched Swiss pairing.
limitations: Official Annex tables cover the recorded range; structural behavior outside that range is not an official-example comparison.
Reversing the last two rounds in a double round robin is a recommendation exposed as an option, not a mandatory rule.
C.05 parent §5.1/§5.3 pointers are retained as unresolved prior-wave claims because the parent page fetch exposed no article text; Annex 2 Varma restricted draws are caller-owned and not implemented.

records.name: Dutch pre-2026 compatibility ruleset
records.scope_note: Frozen compatibility entry point for the older pre-2026 F-0107 Dutch formulation as realized by the v0.1.0 kernel; it is not the interim 2025 F-0106 source and is not current Dutch-2026 behavior. The F-0106 source is indexed separately as source-only because no distinct implementation is claimed. The v0.1.0 golden corpus pins historical repository outputs, not FIDE conformity.
limitations: Historical source mapping is not clause-complete; F-0106 interim-2025 is a separate recovered source-only record, not a claimed compatibility target.
Known legacy deviations remain; the v0.1.0 golden corpus is a repository compatibility oracle, not an independent FIDE oracle.

records.name: Tournament Handler Program (THP) product boundary
records.scope_note: FIDE C.02.03 defines a THP as an application managing player data, pairings and results and requires product features beyond this pairing-only library. FIDE list evidence is bounded to the retrieved C.02.04 page.
limitations: Pairing-Core has no THP evaluation, TAPC, FIDE approval or endorsement claim.
Absence from a retrieved list does not rule out an unobserved later written decision.

records.name: C.07 tie-break calculation boundary
records.scope_note: Tie-break calculations belong to a separate library/application. C.07 results are not silently substituted for the C.04.4.2 Burstein Index.
limitations: No C.07 calculator is implemented in Pairing-Core.
No semantic equivalence between C.07 and C.04 Burstein calculations has been verified.

records.name: Knockout/play-off pairing boundary
records.scope_note: Play-off format and event orchestration are tournament-regulation responsibilities and are not a Pairing-Core engine.
limitations: No knockout or play-off engine is implemented.

records.name: Dutch interim 2025 edition — source-only historical record
records.scope_note: Historical C.04.3 source edition only; no runnable ruleset or implementation is claimed. The official Council PDF states application from 2025-07-01, but its approval-date field is the placeholder dd/mm/yyyy. The F-0107 frozen compatibility system and current F-0105 Dutch-2026 system remain separate.
limitations: The Table of Changes describes C9 as intended to prevent missed-game players from receiving a PAB; the operative C5/C9 text is a minimization criterion, not a categorical fewer-games exclusion.
No Pairing-Core implementation or named repository test maps specifically to this interim edition; any owner request for it requires a distinct versioned ruleset and tests.
